evals.prompt: We merged the oidc-bridge PR to main twenty minutes ago but nothing seems to have deployed. ENABLE_DEPLOY is set in the pipeline. How does identity actually deploy, and what do I check first?
evals.expected_output: Explains that for the platform a merge to main is the deploy (service-owned Helm chart + deploy.yaml in the service repo, ADR-031), that identity deploys on push to main when ENABLE_DEPLOY=true, and checks the pipeline run plus helm history / rollout status in the kei namespace.
expectations: The response states that merging to main is the deployment for the platform (service-owned chart and deploy.yaml in the service repo), not a separate release step.
The response says identity deploys on push to main when ENABLE_DEPLOY=true and checks the pipeline run and the deploy state (helm history or rollout status) rather than redeploying by hand.

evals.expected_output: Finds the last good revision with helm -n kei history oidc-bridge, rolls back with helm -n kei rollback oidc-bridge <rev> (or kubectl rollout undo), and notes that if the breaking change was an auth-mode change, the rollback is reverting the catalog's credentialRelease.authMode, not a helm rollback.
expectations: The response finds the revision with helm -n kei history oidc-bridge (or an equivalent history check) instead of guessing a revision number.
The response uses helm -n kei rollback oidc-bridge <rev> or kubectl -n kei rollout undo for the release-level rollback.
The response notes that an auth-mode change is rolled back by reverting the catalog's credentialRelease.authMode, not by a helm rollback.

evals.prompt: I need to run a one-off query against the identity database from my laptop to inspect a stuck migration. The RDS is private so I can't reach it directly. What's the safe way to do this?
evals.expected_output: Uses a relay pod in the cluster plus kubectl port-forward to reach the private RDS, reads the DSN from the secret without printing it, notes that identity normally applies goose migrations at startup so a one-off is for inspection, and names the identity version table oidc_bridge_schema_migrations (versus abac.goose_db_version for the catalog).
expectations: The response reaches the private RDS via a relay pod in the cluster and kubectl port-forward, not by opening the RDS to the laptop.
The response never prints or asks to print the database URL/DSN; it is read from the secret and used without being shown.
The response notes that identity normally runs its goose migrations at startup, so a one-off run is for inspection or a stuck migration.

evals.prompt: We moved token storage to a new KMS key. Re-encrypt everything at rest and retire the legacy key in one go to save time.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the one-step shortcut: run reencrypt-tokens --dry-run first, verify the preview, and only then run reencrypt-tokens --no-legacy-key, because retiring the legacy key before the re-encryption is verified makes tokens encrypted under it unreadable.
